_note: Sites triaged as acceptable fail-open reads, each with a reason a reader can check against the source -- the same convention as tools/reachability_exemptions.json. Keyed on (file, var) rather than line: line numbers shift on every edit and a stale line silently un-accepts an entry. The cost is that two variables of the same name in one file are accepted together, so check that before adding one. An entry that matches nothing is reported as STALE by the checker rather than ignored -- the first entry ever written here was resolved within the hour and nothing would otherwise have said so.

reason: ACCEPTED. The failure is already surfaced, not swallowed: `console.error` fires on !w.ok and the function returns `counted: w.ok`, so a caller is told in the return value whether this call was actually recorded. The fallback only affects rowId, which is a best-effort handle for the later usage measurement -- a statistic, never a control.

ACCEPTED, with the consequence stated. The value feeds excludeCredentials, the WebAuthn list telling an authenticator not to enrol a passkey it already holds. A failed read means the list is empty, so a user could register a SECOND passkey on the same authenticator. That is a duplicate credential row, not an access grant: no new person gains entry, nothing is overwritten, and multiple passkeys per employee are a normal and wanted state anyway. Refusing registration because a read failed would be the worse trade.

ACCEPTED, and already deliberately handled. The file carries its own comment: a bare ternary made a failing read indistinguishable from an unpublished profile, so a console.error was added on !sr.ok. The value is the shop's optional contact block on a public order-tracking page; its absence degrades the page rather than asserting anything false, and the failure is now in the log where an operator can see it.

ACCEPTED, and the direction is why. findIcd10Match() does `if (!r.ok) return null` on a public NLM ICD-10 lookup. Surfaced 2026-09-04 the first time this tool's default walk included app HTML. Both consumers were read, not assumed. sairncode.html:6598 turns a null into `{source:'none'}` -- a VERIFICATION source, so an unreachable API reports the code as UNVERIFIED rather than verified: it under-claims, which is the safe direction for a coding tool. sairncode.html:11774 falls through to a web-search tier whose own prompt says 'never invent a plausible-sounding code number'. Neither consumer reads null as 'no such code exists'. The function's comment states the rule it is keeping -- 'never invents a code if the API returns nothing' -- and the code keeps it. NOT accepted as a general licence for `if (!r.ok) return null` in this file: this is one function whose two call sites were both checked.

ACCEPTED 2026-09-08 after reading the retry loop, which is the question the open-work row asked and did not answer. This is the RE-READ before a retry: reRows feeds `const reRow = (Array.isArray(reRows) && reRows[0]) || null;` and the very next statement is `if (!reRow) { 409 WRITE_CONFLICT ... 'the record could not be re-read. Nothing was saved' }`. So a failed read FAILS CLOSED, refuses the write, and the refusal message names the real reason rather than blaming a conflict that may not exist. The checker matches the ternary shape; the null flows into an explicit guard that refuses, which is the shape this sweep converts things TO.

ACCEPTED 2026-09-08, and it is the OPPOSITE of reRows above by design -- worth stating because the two are three lines apart and identical to the checker. This one is the WRITE's echo, not an input: the guard is `if (!writeR.ok || (Array.isArray(secondRows) && secondRows.length === 0))`, so an unreadable BODY on a 2xx does not refuse. That is correct -- the write landed; only the server's echo of the saved row was lost. The response then reports `publicStatus((savedRow && savedRow.data) || applyChange(reRow.data))`, and that fallback is the exact blob this request just wrote against the re-read row, which is what the author's own comment above it requires ("the response must describe THAT blob, not the stale `next`"). A read that cannot be read is a failure; a write that succeeded but could not be echoed is not.

ACCEPTED 2026-09-08. This is the app's own data wrapper, not a decision: `grdData()` ends `if (!res.ok) return null; var j = await res.json(); return (j && j.ok) ? j : null;` and returning null on any failure IS the platform contract every app's xData() implements -- the checker's own header calls that the shape this sweep converts things TO. The real question is whether CALLERS act on the null, and that was measured rather than assumed: 36 of 45 call sites in this file read the result. The remaining 9 are fire-and-forget, which is the separate discard-the-result class the storage-wrapper and write-failure-voice work covers -- NOT a fail-open in this wrapper, and NOT cleared by this entry. Also checked while here: the false "server sync not yet enabled for this app" message is now absent from every app file, so a failure in this wrapper no longer surfaces a wrong reason anywhere.
